title: Create, edit, and manage scripts
description: Learn how the Quickque library, full-content search, selection, bulk actions, Trash, sorting, and custom order work.
body:
# Create, edit, and manage scripts

Quickque treats a script as a title plus an ordered list of sections. The current library also supports full-content search, a workspace home page, Trash, sorting, and a custom order. Those controls stay local to the browser origin or desktop app where you use them.

## Before you begin

- Open the library in Quickque.
- Keep a full backup before a large reorganization, moving scripts to Trash, or permanently deleting anything. Use **Settings & backups** → **Export Full Backup**; [Backup, restore, and migration](/guide/backup-restore/) explains the versioned JSON file.
- Remember that the library is local to this browser origin or desktop app. It is not synchronized between them.

## Steps

1. Select **New script** on the workspace home page, then choose **Presentation** for talks or **Performance / Self-tape** for a scene. For Presentation, the new entry is **Untitled Presentation**, with **Section 1** ready to edit. If no script is selected, the editor also offers **Create Script**.

2. Edit the script title in the large title field. Quickque saves edits to the local library as you work.

3. Edit a section title and its text directly in the editor. Select **Add Section** for another beat. Each section has its own title and text area.

4. Reorder sections with the up and down controls in a section header. Use the trash control in that header to delete a section. Quickque keeps at least one section in a script.

5. Use the **Search scripts…** field in the library to filter live scripts by title, section title, or section content. Search is local and case-insensitive. In Trash, the same search field searches the deleted scripts there.

6. Select the sort control, initially labeled **Custom Order**, to choose **Newest First**, **Oldest First**, **Title A-Z**, **Title Z-A**, or **Custom Order**. The selected sort mode is saved with the library.

7. For **Custom Order**, clear the search field, then use an item's **Move Up** and **Move Down** actions. Script rows in the editor sidebar can also be dragged. Reordering changes the saved custom order; it does not rewrite script text.

8. Open a script's options menu for **Rename**, **Duplicate**, **Export as TXT**, **Export as JSON**, or **Move to Trash**. A duplicate is titled with **(Copy)** and receives independent script and section identifiers; editing it does not edit the original.

9. Moving a script to Trash opens a confirmation such as **Move 1 script to Trash?**. Confirming removes it from Library but keeps it on this device. Open **Trash** to use **Restore** or **Delete Permanently** from an item's options menu. Permanent deletion is explicitly irreversible. Trash has no automatic expiry.

10. Each workspace card has **Edit** and **Present** or **Rehearse** actions. Edit opens the script editor; Present or Rehearse opens playback directly, with performance setup checked first. You can also select Present or Rehearse from the editor. The reader's section selector lets you navigate the saved section order without changing the library's script order.

![Quickque library in the browser preview](/images/library.webp)

*Browser preview only: this screenshot shows the library/editor labels and is not native-app evidence.*

## Edit the whole script in Markdown

Select **Markdown** in the editor to write the full script in one pane. Use `# Script title`, `## Section or turn title`, `**Alex:**` for a character’s dialogue, and `> Stage direction` for notes. Each character cue begins a turn; existing character names retain their In Person / AI Partner assignments, colours and voices. New names create AI Partners that you can configure in Scene Partner. Prefix markup with a backslash to speak it literally.

Select **Save script** to update the section editor. Invalid markup leaves your draft open with an error; **Back to sections** asks before discarding unsaved edits.

## Performance and self-tape setup

A new performance starts as **Untitled Performance** with **Turn 1**. Use **Add Turn** to add dialogue. Open **Scene Partner** to add cast, assign **In Person** to each character you perform and **AI Partner** to characters Quickque reads, and choose and preview local voices for the other characters. Assign a character to every turn and keep stage directions in **Notes**. All AI Partner means a full read-through; all In Person gives silent turn cues. Choose a colour accent for each character to recognise their turns.

Choose **Rehearse**. With **Partner audio** enabled, Quickque checks dialogue, assignments and local partner voices before opening the reader. Select a setup issue to fix it. If no local voice is available, assign every character as **In Person** for silent turn cues, or switch **Partner audio** off to read at your own pace. Turning audio off keeps your performance type and cast. **Script type** switches between Presentation and Performance without deleting dialogue or cast.

Record a self-tape on a separate camera. Quickque does not record audio or video. Native scene audio still requires physical Mac verification.

## Expected result

The workspace shows script preview cards, **Edit**, **Present** or **Rehearse**, full-content search, **Trash**, and the selected sorting label. The editor preserves your section order and text. Duplicate creates an independent copy. Move to Trash is recoverable; **Restore** returns a script to Library, while **Delete Permanently** removes a trashed script without a recovery path. A full backup includes live scripts, active selection, Trash, custom order, and sorting mode.

## Troubleshooting

- **Search returns No scripts found:** search includes script titles, section titles, and section text. Clear **Search scripts…** or **Search Trash…**, or change the words you are looking for.
- **I cannot reorder scripts:** choose **Custom Order** and clear the search field. Dragging and **Move Up**/**Move Down** are disabled while another sort mode or a filtered search is active.
- **I opened the wrong script:** return to Workspace and select **Edit** on the intended card.
- **A script disappeared after deletion:** it was likely moved to **Trash**, not permanently erased. Open **Trash** and choose **Restore**.
- **A duplicate changed the original:** check that you edited the copied library item, whose title ends in **(Copy)**. A duplicate has its own section IDs.
- **The title says Untitled Presentation:** select the title field and replace it; this is a normal initial value, not a failed save.
- **An error says the library could not be saved:** stop making destructive changes, keep the current data open, and retry only after the storage problem is understood. A failed library write keeps the previous durable library, Trash, selection, and sort state unchanged.
- **A script is present in one place but not another:** browser storage and Tauri app storage are separate. Use **Export Full Backup** and **Import Backup JSON** for migration rather than expecting automatic sync.
